consumer.text: Everything you want to watch is on your computer. And your computer isn't on the sofa.
VidVNC brings it to your TV, or any portable device. Smooth, sharp, and with sound.
Open VidVNC on your Mac or PC, and it shows you a code.
Scan it with your phone, or type it into your TV's browser. There's nothing to install.
Use your phone, your tablet, or a compatible smart TV.
Want to do more than watch? Take over the mouse and keyboard without leaving the sofa. On a phone, just use your finger.
It all stays on your home network, it's encrypted, and nothing connects until you say so.
VidVNC. Your computer, on every screen in the house.

developer.text: Traditional VNC sends your screen as a series of still pictures.
So you click, and wait. You drag a window, and watch it catch up.
VidVNC streams your desktop as video instead, with sound.
Same computer, same network. It just keeps up.
About sixty-three milliseconds, screen to screen, at 1080p. And it scales up to 4K, so text stays crisp.
developer.caption: About 63 milliseconds, screen to screen, at 1080p. And it scales up to 4K, so text stays crisp.

developer.text: Type, scroll, switch windows. It keeps up, so you stay focused on the work.
To connect, open VidVNC and show a code.
Scan it, or type the short key. The viewer runs in the browser, so there's nothing to install.
Devices you use every day can register once and sign in with a username and password, if you allow it. Passkeys are coming in a later release.
The keyboard and mouse are only handed over when you say so.
It runs on Mac and Windows, and encodes on the graphics hardware, so your processor stays free for real work.
Speed is half the job. The other half is keeping it safe.
VidVNC is split into parts, and each part only gets the access it needs.
Network traffic arrives at a single guarded port, and only verified senders get through.
The video connection runs in a sandbox. Break into it, and you still can't see the screen, send input, or read files.
It talks to the trusted side only through narrow pipes, and screen capture never touches the network.
Connections are encrypted, remote access is off until you turn it on, and every code works once.
VidVNC. Your desktop, in real time, on your network.
